svg.title: How a streaming chat request becomes server-sent events
svg.desc: After the same middleware as POST /chat, the stream route refuses with 409 a caller that does not hold the thread's lease and, without an Idempotency-Key, a thread that already has a durable run in flight. It resolves and pins the manifest and screens the user's messages. Under an Idempotency-Key the first request claims the key and a repeat replays what the first one streamed instead of running again. It then branches on spec.execution.mode. A durable manifest starts a fiber and streams the run's progress, run_accepted then run_status on each change then final, with the session events the worker appends tailed in between. A transient one compiles the agent and streams its events with a keep-alive comment after fifteen quiet seconds. Structural frames carry an id, the thread's next session sequence, which a client hands back as Last-Event-ID to GET /chat/stream/{thread_id} after a dropped connection.
